question: From the given alternatives, which part of the flower finally changes into a fruit in the flowering plant?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Ovary**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In flowering plants, the **ovary** is the basal, swollen part of the **carpel** (or **pistil**), which serves as the female reproductive organ.
 
• After the process of **fertilization** occurs, the **ovary** undergoes a series of biological transformations and eventually matures into a **fruit**. ***Hence, the correct answer is Ovary.***
 
• This transformation is primarily driven by the secretion of plant hormones such as **auxins**, **gibberellins**, and **ethylene**, which stimulate the growth and ripening of the ovarian tissues.
 
• The wall of the **ovary** develops into the **pericarp**, which constitutes the external skin and the fleshy part of the **fruit**.
 
• During this stage of the plant's life cycle, other floral parts such as the **sepals**, **petals**, and **stamens** generally wither and fall off, although in some species, the **calyx** may persist.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Ovule and Seed Development:**

 
 
• The **ovules**, which are housed inside the **ovary**, contain the female gametes. Following successful **fertilization**, these **ovules** develop into **seeds**.
 
• The protective layers of the **ovule**, known as **integuments**, harden to form the **seed coat** (**testa** and **tegmen**).
 
 
 
• **Classification of Fruits:**
 
 
• **True Fruits:** These are **fruits** that develop exclusively from the **mature ovary**. Examples include **Mango**, **Grape**, and **Tomato**.
 
• **False Fruits (Accessory Fruits):** These develop from the **ovary** along with other floral parts like the **thalamus** or **receptacle**. Common examples are **Apple**, **Pear**, and **Strawberry**.
 
• **Parthenocarpic Fruits:** In some cases, a **fruit** develops without **fertilization**. This process is called **parthenocarpy**, and the resulting **fruits** (such as **Banana** and certain varieties of **Grapes**) are typically seedless.
 
 
 
• **Angiosperms:**
 
 
• Flowering plants are classified as **Angiosperms**. Their defining characteristic is the production of **seeds** enclosed within a **fruit**, unlike **Gymnosperms** where **seeds** are naked.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Structure of the Carpel:** A typical **carpel** consists of three main parts: the **stigma** (receives pollen), the **style** (the tube-like structure), and the **ovary** (the base containing **ovules**).
 
• **The Pericarp:** The **pericarp** is often differentiated into three distinct layers: the **epicarp** (outer skin), **mesocarp** (middle fleshy layer), and **endocarp** (inner layer surrounding the **seed**).
 
• **Double Fertilization:** A unique feature of **angiosperms** where one male gamete fuses with the egg to form a **zygote** (**2n**), and the other fuses with the **polar nuclei** to form the **Primary Endosperm Nucleus** (**3n**), which provides nutrition to the developing embryo.
 
• **Seed Dispersal:** The primary evolutionary function of the **fruit** is to protect the **seeds** and aid in their **dispersal** through various agents like **animals**, **wind**, or **water**.
